en: The Theravāda Vinaya Mahāvibhaṅga:
The Chapter on Saṅghādisesa Offenses
1. The Training Rule on Emission of Semen.
Venerable sirs, these thirteen rules involving formal meeting of the Saṅgha come up for recitation.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the Venerable Seyyasaka was leading the holy life without delight.
Because of this, he became thin, haggard, discolored, and pale, with veins showing all over his body.
The Venerable Udāyī saw the Venerable Seyyasaka—thin, haggard, discolored, and pale, with veins showing all over his body—and having seen him, he said this to the Venerable Seyyasaka:
“Friend Seyyasaka, why are you so emaciated, haggard, discolored, and pale, with your veins standing out all over your body?
Are you, friend Seyyasaka, not practicing the holy life with dissatisfaction?
“It is so, friend,” he replied.
“In that case, friend Seyyasaka, eat as much as you like, sleep as much as you like, and bathe as much as you like.

Having eaten as much as you like, slept as much as you like, and bathed as much as you like, whenever dissatisfaction arises in you and lust agitates your mind, then by means of your hand, apply yourself and discharge the semen.
“Friend, is it allowable to do such a thing?”
“Yes, friend. I do the same,” he replied.
Then the Venerable Seyyasaka ate as much as he wished, slept as much as he wished, and bathed as much as he wished.
Having eaten, slept, and bathed as much as he wished, whenever dissatisfaction arose and lust overcame his mind, he would then manually stimulate himself and discharge semen.
Then, after some time, the Venerable Seyyasaka became handsome, with bright faculties, a clear complexion, and a radiant skin tone.
Then the monks who were companions of the Venerable Seyyasaka said this to him:
"Formerly, friend Seyyasaka, you were thin, haggard, discolored, jaundiced, and your limbs were covered with visible veins."
"So now, at this time, you are handsome, with full faculties, a serene facial complexion, and a clear skin tone.
What medicine, friend Seyyasaka, are you taking?
"I am not taking any medicine, friend."
“Moreover, I eat as much as I need, I sleep as much as I need, and I bathe as much as I need.

Having eaten as much as I need, slept as much as I need, and bathed as much as I need, whenever dissatisfaction arises in me and lust agitates my mind, I then take hold with my hand and discharge the impurity.
“But, friend Seyyasaka, do you discharge the impurity with the very same hand with which you eat what has been given in faith?”
“Yes, friends,” they replied.
Then those monks who were of few desires... [and so on]... complained, grumbled, and became indignant, saying:
“How can the Venerable Seyyasaka, by manual effort, discharge semen?”
Then those bhikkhus, having rebuked the venerable Seyyasaka in many ways, reported this matter to the Blessed One.
Then the Blessed One, on this occasion and in this connection, having convened the Saṅgha of bhikkhus, questioned the venerable Seyyasaka:
“Is it true, Seyyasaka, that you discharged semen by means of manual effort?”
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him:
“It is unbecoming, foolish man, it is unwholesome, it is improper, it is unworthy of a recluse, it is unbefitting, it is not to be done.”
"How indeed, foolish man, could you discharge semen by means of manual effort?
Has not the Dhamma, foolish man, been taught by me in many ways for the sake of dispassion, not for the sake of passion;
the Dhamma has been taught for the sake of disentanglement, not for the sake of entanglement?"
The Dhamma has been taught for the sake of non-clinging, not for the sake of clinging.

In this matter, you foolish man, when the Dhamma has been taught by me for the fading away of lust, you intend it with lust; when the Dhamma has been taught for disentanglement, you intend it with entanglement; when the Dhamma has been taught for non-clinging, you intend it with clinging.
Have I not, foolish man, taught the Dhamma in many ways for the fading away of lust, for the intoxication-freeing of intoxication?
Has the Dhamma been taught for the removal of thirst, for the uprooting of attachment, for the cutting off of the cycle of existence, for the destruction of craving, for dispassion, for cessation,
and for Nibbāna? Have I not, O foolish man, declared in many ways the abandoning of sensual pleasures and the full understanding of perceptions of sensual pleasure?
“The removal of thirst for sensual pleasures has been declared; the uprooting of thoughts of sensual pleasure has been declared; the subsiding of the fever of sensual pleasure has been declared.
This, foolish man, does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence, nor to the increase of the confidence of those who already have it.
On the contrary, foolish man, this leads to the lack of confidence in those without confidence, and to the alienation of some of those who already have confidence.”
Then the Blessed One, having rebuked the venerable Seyyasaka in many ways for being difficult to support...
[and so forth] ...and furthermore, monks, you should recite this training rule:
"Intentional emission of semen is an offense entailing suspension (saṅghādisesa)."
Thus was this training rule laid down by the Blessed One for the monks.
Now at that time, after eating fine foods, the monks fell asleep with muddled mindfulness and lacking clear comprehension.
As they fell asleep with muddled mindfulness and lacking clear comprehension, semen was emitted during a dream.
They became anxious, thinking:
"The Blessed One has laid down a training rule:
'Intentional emission of semen is an offense entailing suspension (saṅghādisesa).'"
“Unchastity was emitted by us even in a dream,
and there was volition involved in it.
Have we perhaps incurred an offense entailing suspension (saṅghādisesa)?”
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Bhikkhus, there is such an intention,
and yet it is not to be designated.”
And so, monks, you should recite this training rule:
“Intentional emission of semen, except during a dream, is an offense entailing suspension (saṅghādisesa).
“Intentional” means:
Transgression occurs when one knows, perceives, intends, and resolves.
"Whites" refers to the ten white [deeds].
Blue, yellow, red, white, the color of buttermilk, the color of water, the color of oil, the color of milk, the color of curd, and the color of ghee.
"Emission" (vissaṭṭhī) is said to mean causing to fall from its place; thus it is called emission.
"Except in a dream" means excluding what occurs during sleep.
"Saṅghādisesa" [is as defined previously].
The Saṅgha alone grants probation for that offense, sends back to the beginning, grants the trial period (mānatta), or rehabilitates; neither a group nor a single individual does so.
Therefore it is called a “Saṅghādisesa. This is the naming and designation of that very class of offenses. For this reason also it is called a “Saṅghādisesa.
